title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 5.87 (versions follow prime numbers; 587 after 577): what her customs do not cover, she answers with what her books say. A custom answers only what it covers: a word said to her is covered when some example says a word of its kind (the same, or one in the same hole); the one that stands where no example has anything is what she is asked about, and she looks in her books for the sentences that are about it (the word is the first that counts in the sentence, it ends as a sentence and says at least one more word that counts), up to seven, in the order of her reading. They go where her examples always go: the first she has not said yet, then her school's song, then her luck. Seen in a hidden copy: three questions about a character of the book she was reading, three different sentences about her. Also: seven science books on her shelf (223 whole articles of the Spanish Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0) and her logo, shown large while she wakes. She says the first sentence she finds, not the best one; those questions take up to 17 seconds. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v5.57: Luma purificada. Prototipo de investigación.
